projects.name: Analytics Dashboard Platform
projects.description:
End-to-end analytics dashboard delivering three capability pillars: (1) customer CSV data ingestion and processing, (2) application log analysis, and (3) visualization components with an interactive dashboard UI. Scope covers discovery through production release, including data modeling, a metrics/semantic layer, and operational readiness.

Tags: analytics, data-pipeline, csv-ingestion, log-analysis, visualization, dashboard

tasks.name: M1 — Discovery, Requirements & Data Source Audit
tasks.details: Establish the factual ground truth for the project before any build work: inventory the customer CSV exports (schemas, delimiters, encodings, volumes, refresh cadence, known quality defects), inventory the application log sources (formats, severity scales, retention, sample access), and capture the stakeholder questions the dashboard must answer. Output: a signed-off requirements + data audit pack that the pipeline and visualization work can be designed against. No production data is transformed in this milestone.

tasks.name: M3 — Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing Pipeline
tasks.details: Build the batch pipeline that lands customer CSV files and turns them into trustworthy, query-ready customer records: file intake and landing zone, schema validation and drift detection, cleansing and normalization, idempotent loading, and data quality gates with quarantine handling. Output: a scheduled, monitored pipeline whose outputs reconcile against source row counts.

tasks.name: M4 — Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that parses application logs into structured events and derives operational analytics: log collection and shipping, parsing/field extraction, severity and error classification, deduplication and sessionization, and aggregation into error-rate, latency, and usage metrics. Output: a reliable log analytics dataset with defined freshness SLAs and alert thresholds.

tasks.name: M5 — Data Storage, Modeling & Metrics Layer
tasks.details: Unify the CSV and log streams into a governed analytics model: storage layout and partitioning, canonical dimensions and facts, slowly changing dimensions for customer attributes, and a documented metrics/semantic layer so every dashboard number has one authoritative definition. Output: an agreed metric catalogue with owners, formulas, grains, and freshness, backed by tested warehouse models.

tasks.name: M6 — Visualization Components & Dashboard Experience
tasks.details: Design and build the user-facing layer: information architecture and wireframes, a reusable chart component library bound to the metrics layer, the customer analytics and log/operational views, filtering and drill-down interactions, and accessibility plus responsive layout. Output: a usable dashboard application whose tiles trace back to documented metrics and meet agreed performance budgets.

tasks.name: M7 — Quality Assurance, Security, Launch & Operations
tasks.details: Prove the platform is fit to run: end-to-end and reconciliation testing, performance/load validation, access control and PII handling review, runbooks and on-call ownership, staged rollout, and post-launch monitoring with a defined rollback path. Output: production launch with verified SLAs, documented support model, and a tracked post-launch review.

tasks.name: M2 — Platform Architecture, Environments & Delivery Foundation
tasks.details: Define how the dashboard is built and shipped: component architecture, technology choices, data flow boundaries, environment topology (dev/staging/prod), CI/CD, code repository and conventions, secrets management, and observability baseline. Output: an architecture decision record set plus a working deployable skeleton so downstream milestones build into a real pipeline rather than throwaway scripts.

tasks.name: M1.1 Stakeholder interviews & decision-question catalogue
tasks.details: Interview the requesting teams and record, for each: the decision they intend to make, the metric that informs it, the time grain, the comparison baseline, and the acceptable data freshness. Produce a prioritised list of dashboard questions (must-have vs. later) with a named owner per question. Deliverable: decision-question catalogue (~1 page per domain) approved by the stakeholders.

tasks.name: M1.2 Customer CSV source inventory & schema profiling
tasks.details: For every customer CSV export: record origin system, delivery mechanism, refresh cadence, file size and row volume, delimiter, encoding, header structure, column definitions, primary/foreign keys, and example values. Profile a representative sample for null rates, duplicates, format inconsistencies, and unexpected schema variants. Deliverable: CSV source inventory spreadsheet plus a written schema profile per file family.

tasks.name: M1.3 Application log source inventory & format profiling
tasks.details: Enumerate log sources (app servers, workers, gateway, scheduled jobs): log format (JSON/linesyslog/plaintext), available fields, timestamp format and timezone, severity vocabulary, retention window, volume per day, and access method. Sample each source and count parse-failure risks such as multi-line stack traces and embedded newlines. Deliverable: log source inventory with a sample fixture file checked in per format.

tasks.name: M1.4 Data quality defect register & remediation priorities
tasks.details: Consolidate the defects found in CSV and log profiling into a single register: defect, affected source, frequency, downstream impact, detection method, proposed remediation, and whether it blocks a must-have question from M1.1. Rank by impact vs. effort. Deliverable: prioritised defect register with an explicit accept/mitigate/quarantine decision per defect.

tasks.name: M1.5 Requirements & data audit sign-off pack
tasks.details: Assemble the catalogues, schemas, inventories, and defect register into one requirements pack covering scope, out-of-scope, must-have metrics, data freshness targets, and known constraints. Circulate for review, resolve comments, and obtain written sign-off from the business owner and the data owner. Deliverable: approved requirements pack that later milestones are measured against.

tasks.name: M2.1 Architecture decision records & component diagram
tasks.details: Decide and document: ingestion mechanism, storage engine, transformation tooling, orchestration scheduler, BI/frontend framework, and hosting model. For each decision record context, options considered, trade-off, and consequence. Include a component and data-flow diagram showing CSV and log paths converging on the metrics layer. Deliverable: ADR set (~5 records) plus current-state architecture diagram.

tasks.name: M2.2 Repository, IaC skeleton & environment topology
tasks.details: Create the monorepo layout (ingestion / transforms / dashboards / infra), branch strategy, lint and formatting rules, and infrastructure-as-code definitions for dev, staging, and prod with isolated storage and credentials. Stand up dev end-to-end and verify a hello-world job can deploy. Deliverable: repository with IaC for three environments and a README describing topology.

tasks.name: M2.3 CI/CD pipeline with build, test and deploy stages
tasks.details: Implement automated checks on every change: linting, unit tests, SQL/transform tests, and artifact build; then promote to staging on merge to main and to prod on an approved release tag. Add a rollback path and deployment status notification. Deliverable: green CI/CD pipeline demonstrated by deploying the skeleton to staging and prod.

tasks.name: M2.4 Secrets management & access baseline
tasks.details: Move all credentials into a managed secret store, grant least-privilege roles per environment and per pipeline component, define service accounts, and enable audit logging for secret access. Document rotation procedure. Deliverable: no secrets in source control verified by a scanner, plus a short access matrix.

tasks.name: M2.5 Observability baseline for pipelines and dashboard
tasks.details: Instrument the skeleton with structured logging, job success/failure events, run duration, and row-count metrics; wire a shared alerting channel with one test alert per severity. Define the on-call escalation stub. Deliverable: a dashboard of pipeline health plus a verified test alert reaching the on-call channel.

tasks.name: M3.1 Landing zone & file intake contract
tasks.details: Define and implement the drop location and naming convention for incoming CSVs, plus a manifest recording file name, source, checksum, byte size, arrival timestamp, and expected row count. Reject and alert on files that violate the contract or repeat a checksum already processed. Deliverable: intake handler plus written file contract document.

tasks.name: M3.2 CSV parser handling delimiters, encodings and quoting
tasks.details: Implement a parser that auto-detects or is configured per source for delimiter, quote and escape characters, encoding (UTF-8/UTF-16/latin-1), header presence, and embedded newlines in quoted fields. Emit every row as a raw record with source line number retained for traceability. Deliverable: parser with unit tests over one fixture per known format variant.

tasks.name: M3.3 Schema validation & drift detection
tasks.details: Encode the expected schema per file family as a contract (column names, types, nullability, allowed enums). Compare every incoming file against the contract; classify differences as compatible additions, renames, or breaking changes; block breaking changes and raise a drift alert naming the changed column. Deliverable: validator with a test case per drift class.

tasks.name: M3.4 Cleansing & normalization rules
tasks.details: Implement deterministic transformations: trim and collapse whitespace, standardize date and timestamp parsing to UTC, normalize phone, country and currency formats, canonicalize customer IDs and email casing, and map null-like tokens (empty, N/A, NULL, -) to true nulls. Every rule is documented and unit tested. Deliverable: reusable cleansing module with a rule catalogue.

tasks.name: M3.5 Idempotent merge / upsert loader
tasks.details: Load cleansed records into the customer table using a deterministic business key and a merge strategy so that re-running the same file produces no duplicates and no unintended overwrites. Add a run-id and processed-at watermark per record. Deliverable: loader verified by running the same batch twice and proving row counts and values are unchanged.

tasks.name: M3.6 Data quality gates, quarantine & reprocessing
tasks.details: Implement gate checks per batch: required-field null rate, primary-key uniqueness, referential validity, and accepted value ranges. Rows failing a gate go to a quarantine table with the failing rule and source line; passing rows proceed. Provide a documented reprocessing command that replays quarantined rows after a fix. Deliverable: gate configuration plus quarantine and replay demonstrated on seeded bad rows.

tasks.name: M3.7 Batch reconciliation reporting
tasks.details: Produce a per-batch reconciliation report: rows received, parsed, passed validation, quarantined, inserted, updated, and rejected, with the difference explained and a hard failure if unexplained variance exceeds a configured tolerance. Deliverable: reconciliation report template populated automatically and retained per run.

tasks.name: M3.8 Scheduling & operational monitoring for CSV pipeline
tasks.details: Schedule the pipeline on the agreed cadence, add retries with backoff for transient failures, emit run metrics and a completion/failure notification, and alert when a scheduled run is late or a batch fails its reconciliation tolerance. Deliverable: scheduled job with alerting verified via a forced failure.

tasks.name: M4.1 Log collection & shipping contract
tasks.details: Configure collection from each inventoried source into a raw log store with durable delivery, ordering guarantees where needed, and a documented retention policy. Record source, environment, and ingestion timestamp on every event so raw and parsed layers can be reconciled. Deliverable: collection configuration plus verified continuous delivery from at least one source per format.

tasks.name: M4.2 Log parser & field extraction
tasks.details: Parse each log format into structured fields: timestamp (normalized to UTC), level, service, host, request or trace id, user id, message, duration, status code, and error type. Handle multi-line stack traces by grouping continuation lines into the parent event, and support regex extraction for plaintext formats. Deliverable: parser per format with fixtures covering multi-line and malformed cases.

tasks.name: M4.3 Severity normalization & error taxonomy
tasks.details: Map every source's severity vocabulary (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL and variants such as SEVERE or 5xx) onto one normalized scale, and define an error taxonomy grouping exceptions into stable categories (timeout, auth, validation, dependency, unknown). Document the mapping table and keep unmapped values visible rather than silently dropped. Deliverable: mapping config, taxonomy document, and a count of unmapped values per source.

tasks.name: M4.4 Deduplication & sessionization logic
tasks.details: Remove duplicate log deliveries using a deterministic event fingerprint, and group events into sessions or request traces using trace id where present and an inactivity window otherwise. Handle out-of-order arrival with a bounded lateness window. Deliverable: dedupe and session logic with before/after counts proving removal of retried duplicates without losing distinct events.

tasks.name: M4.5 Aggregation of error-rate, latency and usage metrics
tasks.details: Compute per-minute and per-hour aggregates: total requests, error count and error rate by category, p50/p95/p99 latency from duration fields, throughput, and active session counts. Make grain and windowing explicit and handle empty periods as zero rather than missing. Deliverable: aggregate tables with tests comparing a sample hour against a manual calculation.

tasks.name: M4.6 Log data quality checks & dead-letter handling
tasks.details: Route unparseable records to a dead-letter store with the failure reason and raw payload; monitor parse success rate per source and fail the run when it falls below an agreed threshold. Add checks for stale sources (no events in N minutes) and clock skew. Deliverable: dead-letter store, parse-rate metric, and an alert on threshold breach.

tasks.name: M4.7 Freshness SLA, alert thresholds & scheduling
tasks.details: Agree the freshness target for log metrics with consumers, schedule the pipeline to meet it, and configure thresholds for error-rate spikes, latency regressions, and pipeline staleness with an explicit owner per alert. Deliverable: SLA statement, scheduler configuration, and alert rules verified by simulated breach.

tasks.name: M5.1 Storage layout & partitioning strategy
tasks.details: Define the layered storage zones (raw, cleansed, modeled, serving), naming conventions, and partitioning keys (typically event date and source) with a retention and archival rule per layer. Confirm query patterns drive partition choice by testing a representative range query's scanned bytes. Deliverable: written layout standard plus partition verification result.

tasks.name: M5.2 Customer dimension build
tasks.details: Build the conformed customer dimension from the cleansed CSV layer with a stable surrogate key, a documented business key, and the descriptive attributes the dashboard needs (segment, region, signup date, status, plan). Document grain as one row per customer version and publish column descriptions. Deliverable: dimension table with uniqueness test on the surrogate key.

tasks.name: M5.3 Event fact tables for log activity
tasks.details: Build the fact tables for requests, errors, and sessions from the log aggregates, joined to the customer dimension where an identifiable customer or account id exists and to a date dimension always. Declare grain explicitly (one row per request / per error / per session per hour) and document foreign keys. Deliverable: fact tables with referential integrity tests passing.

tasks.name: M5.4 Slowly changing dimension handling for customer attributes
tasks.details: Implement change tracking so historical metrics keep the attribute values that were true at the time (e.g. a customer who moved region does not retroactively change last quarter's regional totals). Use effective-from and effective-to dates plus a current-flag, and define which attributes are tracked historically versus overwritten. Deliverable: SCD logic with a test proving a changed attribute produces a new version and an unchanged join for history.

tasks.name: M5.5 Metric definition catalogue
tasks.details: For each dashboard metric write one definition containing: plain-language meaning, exact formula, source tables, grain, filters and exclusions, unit, owner, and freshness. Flag and resolve conflicting definitions (for example active customer vs. billed customer). Deliverable: metric catalogue reviewed line by line with stakeholders and version controlled in the repository.

tasks.name: M5.6 Semantic / metrics layer implementation
tasks.details: Implement each catalogued metric once in a shared semantic layer that both the dashboard and ad-hoc consumers query, so the formula lives in one place. Expose dimensions, measures, and default aggregations with consistent names. Deliverable: semantic definitions deployed and a sample query per metric matching the catalogue's expected value on a known reference date.

tasks.name: M5.7 Model tests: uniqueness, referential integrity, freshness
tasks.details: Add automated data tests to every model: primary-key uniqueness and not-null, foreign-key existence against dimensions, accepted values on enums, and freshness assertions against the SLA. Wire the tests into CI so a failing model blocks deployment. Deliverable: test suite green on current data and proven to fail on deliberately corrupted input.

tasks.name: M5.8 Metrics review & stakeholder sign-off
tasks.details: Walk stakeholders through each must-have metric as rendered from the semantic layer, comparing against a known reference figure where one exists, and record agreement or required change. Log any deferred metric as an explicit backlog item rather than an implicit gap. Deliverable: signed metric catalogue v1.0 with a change log.

tasks.name: M6.1 Information architecture & wireframes
tasks.details: Map each must-have question from M1.1 to a specific dashboard page, section, and chart type, and define the navigation model between the customer view and the operational/log view. Produce low-fidelity wireframes stating chart type, axis, grain, and default filters per tile. Deliverable: reviewed wireframe set with a traceability column linking each tile to a metric and a question.

tasks.name: M6.2 Design tokens & dashboard layout shell
tasks.details: Establish the visual foundation: colour palette with accessible contrast, typography scale, spacing grid, KPI and card styles, and light/dark handling if required. Build the responsive page shell with header, filter bar slot, and a grid container that tiles snap into. Deliverable: token file plus a shell page rendering placeholder tiles at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.

tasks.name: M6.3 Chart component library: line, bar, stacked, heatmap, KPI tile
tasks.details: Implement the five required chart primitives as reusable, typed components that accept a data contract (series, categories, units, time grain) rather than hard-coded queries. Include loading, empty, and error states, plus value formatting and tooltips. Deliverable: a component story page showing each chart with fixture data and documented props.

tasks.name: M6.4 Customer analytics dashboard views
tasks.details: Build the customer-facing pages defined in the wireframes: acquisition and signup trend, segment and region breakdown, activity and engagement over time, and a customer detail panel. Bind every tile to a semantic-layer metric, not inline SQL. Deliverable: customer views rendering live data with each tile labelled by its metric definition.

tasks.name: M6.5 Log & operational health dashboard views
tasks.details: Build the operational pages: error rate over time with category breakdown, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput and session volume, top error types, and a recent-errors table with filtering. Include a visible freshness indicator showing the timestamp of the latest processed log event. Deliverable: operational views rendering live log metrics with the freshness indicator working.

tasks.name: M6.6 Global filters, drill-down & cross-filtering
tasks.details: Implement a shared filter state for date range, segment, region, and service, applied consistently to every tile, plus drill-down from an aggregate to its underlying breakdown and a cross-filter that updates peer tiles when a chart element is selected. Filters must be reflected in the URL so a view can be bookmarked and shared. Deliverable: filter and drill behaviour demonstrated end to end with a shareable URL.

tasks.name: M6.7 Accessibility & responsive behaviour
tasks.details: Bring the dashboard to WCAG 2.1 AA: colour contrast on charts and text, keyboard navigation for filters and drill actions, visible focus states, screen-reader labels and data-table alternatives for charts, and layout reflow at narrow widths without horizontal scroll. Deliverable: automated accessibility scan plus a manual keyboard-only walkthrough recorded with issues fixed.

tasks.name: M6.8 Tile query performance tuning & caching
tasks.details: Measure load time per tile against the agreed budget, add result caching with a TTL matched to data freshness, trim over-fetching, and defer below-the-fold tiles. Document the final query and cache strategy. Deliverable: performance report showing each tile within budget on the reference dataset.

tasks.name: M7.1 Automated unit & integration test suites
tasks.details: Raise coverage on the critical paths: CSV parsing, log parsing, cleansing rules, metric formulas, and API endpoints. Add integration tests that run the pipelines against fixture files end to end in an ephemeral environment. Set a coverage floor for changed code in CI. Deliverable: test suites running in CI with a published coverage report.

tasks.name: M7.2 End-to-end reconciliation & user acceptance testing
tasks.details: Load a full production-sized batch and reconcile dashboard totals against source row counts and independently computed control figures. Then run UAT with business users against the must-have question list, recording pass/fail per question and any defect with severity. Deliverable: reconciliation evidence plus a signed UAT result with all critical defects closed.

tasks.name: M7.3 Performance & load testing
tasks.details: Test with production-scale volumes: peak file sizes for CSV ingestion, peak log throughput, and concurrent dashboard users. Record ingest duration, query latency, and tile render time against the agreed budgets, and identify the first bottleneck with a remediation recommendation. Deliverable: load test report with results versus budget.

tasks.name: M7.4 Security review: RBAC, PII handling & retention
tasks.details: Confirm data classification for every dashboard field, apply masking or exclusion for PII in both storage and display, configure role-based access so a viewer sees only permitted segments, and enforce the retention rule with an automated purge. Verify row-level restrictions with test accounts. Deliverable: security review sign-off with access test evidence.

tasks.name: M7.5 Runbooks, SLAs & on-call ownership
tasks.details: Write runbooks for the top failure modes (late file, schema drift, parse-rate drop, failed deployment) with diagnosis steps and recovery commands. Publish the SLA, alert routing, and the named owner for each pipeline and dashboard. Deliverable: runbook set reviewed by the on-call engineer and linked from every alert.

tasks.name: M7.6 Staged rollout & rollback plan
tasks.details: Release to a pilot group first, compare their view against UAT expectations for one full refresh cycle, then expand to all users. Document the rollback trigger, the exact revert steps, and the data-consistency check to run after any revert. Deliverable: executed pilot rollout with go/no-go decision recorded, and a tested rollback.

tasks.name: M7.7 Post-launch monitoring & 30-day review
tasks.details: Watch the first 30 days against SLA: pipeline success rate, freshness, dashboard error rate, and user-reported issues. Collect usage and feedback, then hold a review that records what to fix, what to retire, and what to build next. Deliverable: 30-day review report with prioritised follow-up backlog.
